| 5061 | attifer | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Aussitôt les jeunes gens se réunissent sur la place ; aussitôt les jeunes filles sentent un frisson dans leurs veines, et vite, vite, de s’attifer, de se faire belles, avec le bonnet à rubans et la robe des dimanches ! | At once the young men gather on the square; at once the young women feel a thrill run through them, and quickly, quickly, they dress themselves up, making themselves pretty, with the ribboned bonnet and their Sunday dress! | Lucien Duc, En Provence: Études de mœurs & souvenirs de jeunesse, 1893, d. 1915 |
| 5066 | déterger | tier | verbatim | C'est un petit clystère, un petit clystère, bénin, bénin; il est bénin, bénin: là, prenez, prenez, monsieur; c'est pour déterger, pour déterger, déterger. | It's a little enema, a little enema, mild, mild; it is mild, mild: there, take it, take it, sir; it's meant to cleanse, to cleanse, cleanse. | moliere-oeuvres-t4.txt:14544 |

| 5071 | coqueter | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Lisbeth remarqua cet embarras significatif qui gêne les hommes en présence d’une femme avec laquelle ils se sont interdit de coqueter. | Lisbeth noticed that telltale awkwardness that troubles men in the presence of a woman with whom they have forbidden themselves to flirt. | Honoré de Balzac, La Cousine Bette, 1846, d. 1850 |

| 5084 | bisquer | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Oui, j'ai le spleen, compliqué de la mélancolie, avec la nostalgie, plus l'hypocondrie, et je bisque, et je rage, et je bâille, et je m'ennuie. | Yes, I have the blues, compounded by melancholy, with nostalgia, plus hypochondria, and I sulk, and I rage, and I yawn, and I'm bored. | Victor Hugo, Les Misérables, 1862, d. 1885 |
| 5087 | mixtionner | tier | verbatim | Madame Homais réapparut, portant une de ces vacillantes machines que l'on chauffe avec de l'esprit-de-vin; car Homais tenait à faire son café sur la table, l'ayant d'ailleurs torréfié lui-même, porphyrisé lui-même, mixtionné lui-même. | Madame Homais reappeared, carrying one of those wobbly spirit-lamp contraptions; for Homais insisted on making his coffee at the table, having roasted it himself, ground it himself, and mixed it himself. | flaubert-madame-bovary-1857.txt:13408 |

| 5100 | épointer | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Elle l'écrit partout sur les murs, avec autant de sérieux que s'il s'agissait d'une opération d'importance, et épointe tous mes crayons à ce travail. | She writes it everywhere on the walls, as seriously as if it were a matter of great importance, and blunts every one of my pencils doing it. | Pierre Loti, Aziyadé, 1879, d. 1923 |
| 5112 | pépier | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Les pierrots pépiaient sur les branches gonflées de sève. | The sparrows chirped on the sap-swollen branches. | Émile Gaboriau, L’Argent des autres, 1874, d. 1873 |
| 5113 | cabrioler | tier | verbatim | Mais ils n'apercevaient toujours que ce chapeau, dansant un chahut de tous les diables, cabriolant, tourbillonnant, plongeant et jaillissant. | But all they could see was that hat, dancing a devil of a jig, cavorting, whirling, plunging and springing up again. | zola-lassommoir-1877.txt:15009 |
| 5116 | papilloter | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Je ne sais pas s'il faut attribuer cet effet à la traduction ; mais le cœur me tournait, les yeux me papillotaient, je n'ai pas pu continuer. | I don't know whether the translation was to blame, but my head was spinning, my eyes were swimming, and I couldn't go on. | Honoré de Balzac, Modeste Mignon, 1844, d. 1850 |

| 5123 | trépaner | wiktionary_en | verbatim | Il y a des hommes plutôt faits pour la cueillette, la décoration d'intérieur et les enfants au parc, et des femmes bâties pour aller trépaner le mammouth, faire du bruit et des embuscades. | There are men better suited to gathering, interior decorating, and looking after children at the park, and women built to go trepan the mammoth, make noise, and stage ambushes. | en.wiktionary.org |
| 5124 | courbaturer | tier | verbatim | Le reste des humains m'apparaissait comme bien lointain auprès de cette femme que j'avais quittée il y avait quelques moments à peine; ma joue était chaude encore de son baiser, mon corps courbaturé par le poids de sa taille. | The rest of humanity seemed very distant next to this woman I had left only moments before; my cheek was still warm from her kiss, my body aching from the weight of her frame. | proust-du-cote-de-chez-swann-1913.txt:126 |

| 5130 | remeubler | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Ces deux noms furent dits à l'entrée du boudoir où se trouvait la marquise, jolie pièce récemment remeublée et qui donnait sur le jardin de l'hôtel. | These two names were announced at the entrance to the boudoir where the marquise sat, a pretty room recently refurnished that looked onto the mansion's garden. | Honoré de Balzac, L’Interdiction, 1844, d. 1850 |

| 5147 | estourbir | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Il faut que je sois chez Bras-Rouge à cinq heures avec les Martial pour estourbir la courtière. | I need to be at Bras-Rouge's place at five with the Martials to knock out the broker. | Eugène Sue, Les Mystères de Paris, 1843, d. 1857 |
| 5148 | bruisser | tier | verbatim | Les joncs sifflaient à ras de terre, et les feuilles des hêtres bruissaient en un frisson rapide, tandis que les cimes, se balançant toujours, continuaient leur grand murmure. | The rushes whistled close to the ground, and the beech leaves rustled with a quick shiver, while the treetops, still swaying, kept up their great murmur. | flaubert-madame-bovary-1857.txt:1714 |

| 5181 | ratiociner | tier | verbatim | C'est un miroir qui nous présente naïvement les secrets les plus arcanes de nos individus; et, puisque vous avez la faculté de ratiociner et de parler tout ensemble, à quoi tient-il que vous ne vous serviez de la parole pour me faire entendre votre pensée? | It is a mirror that naively shows us the most hidden secrets of our characters; and since you have the ability to reason pedantically and to speak at the same time, why not use speech to convey your thought to me? | moliere-oeuvres-t2.txt:14949 |

| 5197 | suborner | tier | verbatim | On m'assassine dans le bien, on m'assassine dans l'honneur; et voilà un traître, un scélérat, qui a violé tous les droits les plus saints, qui s'est coulé chez moi sous le titre de domestique, pour me dérober mon argent, et pour me suborner ma fille. | I am being robbed of my property and my honor; and here is a traitor, a scoundrel, who has violated the most sacred rights, who wormed his way into my house under the guise of a servant, to steal my money and to corrupt my daughter. | moliere-oeuvres-t4.txt:12451 |

| 5230 | essarter | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Mais quels obstacles à la surface du sol, et quel travail il aurait fallu pour l'essarter, pour le dégager des orties et des ronces, pour se garantir contre ces milliers d'échardes que le plus léger attouchement leur arrache ! | But what obstacles lay on the ground's surface, and what labor it would have taken to clear it, to free it from nettles and brambles, and to protect oneself from the thousands of splinters the slightest touch would tear loose! | Jules Verne, Le Château des Carpathes, 1892, d. 1905 |

| 5269 | élucubrer | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Du reste, le jour il faisait des tours de force pour vivre, et la nuit il élucubrait un mémoire contre l'évêque de Paris, car il se souvenait d'avoir été inondé par les roues de ses moulins, et il lui en gardait rancune. | Besides, by day he performed astonishing feats just to survive, and by night he dreamed up a treatise against the bishop of Paris, for he remembered being flooded by his mill wheels and still bore him a grudge. | Victor Hugo, Notre-Dame de Paris, 1831, d. 1885 |

| 5328 | rembrunir | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Je suis étonné que les peintres espagnols aient, en général, si fort rembruni leurs tableaux, et se soient jetés presque exclusivement dans l'imitation du Caravage et des maîtres sombres. | I am astonished that Spanish painters have, in general, so darkened their paintings, and thrown themselves almost exclusively into imitating Caravaggio and the somber masters. | Théophile Gautier, Voyage en Espagne, 1859, d. 1872 |
| 5332 | ennuager | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Les glycines à demi défleuries balançaient mélancoliquement leurs grappes d'un mauve pâli ; une pluie matinale avait détrempé les pelouses et ennuagé le ciel. | The half-faded wisterias swayed their pale mauve clusters mournfully; a morning rain had soaked the lawns and clouded the sky. | André Theuriet, Contes de la marjolaine, 1902, d. 1907 |

| 5344 | anathématiser | wiktionnaire | verbatim | L'hérésiarque n'a donc rien à espérer de nos jours, ni des orthodoxes sévères, qui l'anathématiseront, ni des libres penseurs, qui souriront à la tentative de réformer l'irréformable. | The heresiarch, then, has nothing to hope for these days, neither from strict orthodox believers, who will anathematize him, nor from free thinkers, who will merely smile at the attempt to reform the irreformable. | Ernest Renan, L’Avenir de la science, 1890, d. 1892 |

| 5362 | replâtrer | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Le lendemain, dès sept heures, Fougères à son chevalet, retravaillait le tableau condamné ; il en réchauffait la couleur, il y faisait les corrections indiquées par Schinner, il replâtrait ses figures. | The next day, from seven o'clock on, Fougères was back at his easel reworking the condemned painting: he warmed up the color, made the corrections Schinner had suggested, and touched up his figures. | Honoré de Balzac, Pierre Grassou, 1840, d. 1850 |
| 5366 | auner | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Il ne voit rien à fond ; des hommes et des lieux, il en apprend les noms ; des choses, il en apprécie les surfaces ; il a son mètre particulier pour tout auner à sa mesure. | He never sees anything deeply: of men and places he only learns the names; of things he only judges the surface; he has his own yardstick for measuring everything to his own scale. | Honoré de Balzac, L’Illustre Gaudissart, 1834, d. 1850 |
| 5371 | désopiler | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Sur le tréteau d'un saltimbanque, il eût sans doute aisément désopilé le populaire, mais, ici, la robustesse exceptionnelle de ses grands membres était connue, quelques-uns ayant éprouvé, dans les premiers jours, qu'il avait la claque aussi assommante que facile, et les plus malins renfonçaient avec prudence la faribole en leurs gésiers. | On a mountebank's platform, he would no doubt easily have made the crowd laugh, but here the exceptional strength of his big limbs was well known — some had learned early on that his slap was as stunning as it was easy to deliver — and the shrewder ones prudently kept their jokes to themselves. | Léon Bloy, Le grand Polaque, 1893, d. 1917 |
| 5373 | effranger | wiktionnaire | verbatim | — Au milieu s’étend une pelouse où deux fontaines au milieu d’une pièce plate font effranger à leurs vasques une eau qui ne tarit jamais. | In the middle stretches a lawn where two fountains set in a flat pool keep the water at their basins forever rippling into fringe-like patterns that never dry up. | Théophile Gautier, Quand on voyage, 1865, d. 1872 |

| 5378 | autographier | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Si tu m’avais écoutée dans le temps, tu n’aurais pas intercédé pour conserver ton commis principal, et il a sans doute une copie autographiée de ce maudit état ! | If you had listened to me back then, you wouldn't have pleaded to keep your head clerk, and he probably has a facsimile copy of that damned report! | Honoré de Balzac, Les Employés, d. 1850 |
| 5385 | fainéanter | tier | verbatim | Sa voisine, madame Vigouroux, la charbonnière, lui rendait son salut, une petite femme grasse, la face noire, les yeux luisants, fainéantant à rire avec des hommes, adossée contre sa devanture, que des bûches peintes sur un fond lie de vin décoraient d'un dessin compliqué de chalet rustique. | Her neighbor, Madame Vigouroux the coal merchant, returned her greeting — a plump little woman with a grimy face and glistening eyes, idling about laughing with men, leaning against her shop front, which was decorated with an elaborate design of a rustic chalet painted in logs on a wine-lees background. | zola-lassommoir-1877.txt:5292 |

| 5422 | saponifier | wiktionnaire | verbatim | L’ignoble réalité demeurait seule de la coque vide, enlevée à bras d’hommes, jetée dans une voiture, ainsi que ces rebuts de boucherie qu’on emporte, le matin, pour les saponifier dans les fondoirs. | The ignoble reality remained only the empty carcass, carried off by hand, thrown into a cart, like those butcher's scraps that are hauled away each morning to be turned into soap in the rendering vats. | Joris-Karl Huysmans, En route, 1895, d. 1907 |

| 5567 | brillanter | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Ainsi, le poète triomphait de tout obstacle, il brûlait en l’honneur de son amour les bâtons qu’on lui jetait entre les jambes, et Modeste restait ébahie de cet esprit parisien qu’elle ne connaissait pas et qui brillantait les déclamations du discoureur. | So the poet overcame every obstacle, burning in his love's honor the sticks thrown between his legs, and Modeste stood amazed at this Parisian wit she had never known, which gave sparkle to the speaker's declamations. | Honoré de Balzac, Modeste Mignon, 1844, d. 1850 |
| 5568 | rechampir | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Les chambranles des croisées et des portes sont rechampis d’un blanc qui tranche sur les couleurs vives des murailles, et, derrière les vitres, la mousseline suisse étale ses larges ramages. | The window and door frames are picked out in white that stands out against the bright colors of the walls, and behind the panes, Swiss muslin displays its broad patterns. | Théophile Gautier, Ce qu’on peut voir en six jours, 1858, d. 1872 |

| 5636 | compisser | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Le page se plut à renverser le vase de nuit au pied de la muraille par dérision, en disant hautement qu'il compissait le Sorcier et le Chevalier des contes de Marie Coquelière. | The page boy took pleasure in tipping the chamber pot at the foot of the wall in mockery, loudly declaring that he was urinating on the Sorcerer and the Knight of Marie Coquelière's tales. | René Boylesve, La leçon d’amour dans un parc, 1920, d. 1926 |
| 5638 | déhaler | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Après, ils amenèrent des embarcations pour mouiller des ancres, essayer de se déhaler, en réunissant toutes leurs forces sur des amarres — une rude manœuvre qui dura dix heures d'affilée ; — et, le soir venu, le pauvre bateau, arrivé le matin si propre et pimpant, prenait déjà mauvaise figure, inondé, souillé, en plein désarroi. | Afterwards, they brought out boats to lay anchors and try to warp the ship free, pooling all their strength on the mooring lines — a rough maneuver that lasted ten hours straight — and, by evening, the poor boat, which had arrived that morning so clean and spruce, already looked wretched, flooded, fouled, in complete disarray. | Pierre Loti, Pêcheur d’Islande, 1886, d. 1923 |

| 5672 | villégiaturer | tier | verbatim | Il me semble qu’il n’y a pas besoin d’être artiste pour cela et que, même sans flair particulièrement fin, on ne choisit pas d’aller villégiaturer dans des latrines pour être plus à portée de respirer des excréments. | It seems to me one need not be an artist for that, and that even without a particularly fine nose, one does not choose to go and holiday in a latrine in order to be closer to the smell of excrement. | proust-du-cote-de-chez-swann-1913.txt:11140 |

| 5690 | bedonner | wiktionnaire | verbatim | C’était un petit homme chauve, de figure ronde et lippue sans sensualité, et dont le ventre bedonnait sous un gilet de velours à fleurs, défraîchi et de coupe ancienne. | He was a short bald man with a round, thick-lipped face devoid of sensuality, his belly bulging under a faded, old-fashioned flowered velvet waistcoat. | Octave Mirbeau, Les vingt et un Jours d’un neurasthénique, 1901, d. 1917 |
| 5691 | rimailler | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Je rimaillai toujours, malgré le sage conseil de monsieur Mareschal, notre directeur, qui tâcha de me guérir d’une manie malheureusement invétérée, en me racontant dans un apologue les malheurs d’une fauvette tombée de son nid pour avoir voulu voler avant que ses ailes ne fussent poussées. | I went on writing doggerel anyway, despite the wise advice of Monsieur Mareschal, our headmaster, who tried to cure me of an unfortunately ingrained habit by telling me, in the form of a fable, of the misfortunes of a warbler that fell from its nest for wanting to fly before its wings had grown. | Honoré de Balzac, Louis Lambert, 1832, d. 1850 |
| 5692 | désenchaîner | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Il les avait absous au Nom du Père, au Nom du Fils, au Nom de l’Esprit ; il les avait réconciliés, bénis de la bénédiction qui désenchaîne et qui clarifie, de la toute-puissante Bénédiction sacerdotale qui courbe les Neuf Chœurs des Anges. | He had absolved them in the Name of the Father, the Name of the Son, the Name of the Spirit; he had reconciled them, blessed them with the blessing that unchains and purifies, the all-powerful priestly Blessing that bows the Nine Choirs of Angels. | Léon Bloy, Sueur de sang, 1893, d. 1917 |

| 5742 | défriper | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Quand nous descendîmes, la cour de notre auberge était déjà encombrée de charrettes enchevêtrées les unes dans les autres, et des voitures qui arrivaient descendaient des paysans endimanchés qui prenaient leurs femmes dans leurs bras pour les mettre à terre ; alors tout le monde se secouait, les femmes défripaient leurs jupes. | When we got down, our inn's courtyard was already cluttered with carts tangled together, and from arriving carriages came Sunday-dressed peasants lifting their wives to the ground; then everyone shook themselves off, and the women smoothed out their skirts. | Hector Malot, Sans famille, 1878, d. 1907 |

| 5797 | égruger | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Promptement elle ramassa une brassée de bois mort et bientôt elle eut un brasier dans les cendres duquel elle fit cuire un de ses œufs, tandis qu’entre deux silex bien propres et bien polis elle égrugeait une pincée de sel pour qu’il fondît mieux. | She quickly gathered an armful of dead wood and soon had a fire going, in whose embers she cooked one of her eggs, while between two clean, polished flints she ground a pinch of salt so it would dissolve better. | Hector Malot, En famille, 1893, d. 1907 |

| 5809 | vermillonner | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Si la joie d’un bal eût reflété ses teintes rosées sur ce visage pâle ; si les douceurs d’une vie élégante eussent rempli, eussent vermillonné ces joues déjà légèrement creusées ; si l’amour eût ranimé ces yeux tristes, Victorine aurait pu lutter avec les plus belles jeunes filles. | If the joy of a ball had reflected its rosy hues on that pale face; if the comforts of an elegant life had filled out, had flushed with color those cheeks already slightly hollowed; if love had revived those sad eyes, Victorine could have rivaled the loveliest of young women. | Honoré de Balzac, Le Père Goriot, 1835, d. 1850 |
| 5810 | anhéler | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Une fois installé sur ses genoux, il essaya de filer un maigre ronron, mais il l’arrêta, voulut redescendre, glissa lourdement sur ses pattes qui s’écartèrent, demeura immobile, l’échine hérissée, la queue grosse, les oreilles basses ; puis il recommença à fuir dans la chambre et le soufflet de ses flancs anhéla plus fort. | Once settled on his lap, he tried to spin a thin purr, but stopped himself, tried to climb down again, slid heavily on legs that splayed apart, stood motionless, back bristling, tail thick, ears lowered; then he began fleeing about the room again, and the bellows of his flanks panted harder. | Joris-Karl Huysmans, En rade, 1886, d. 1907 |

| 5857 | graillonner | tier | verbatim | La chambre du fond était tout éclairée par les trois brasiers; des roux graillonnaient dans les poêlons, avec une fumée forte de farine brûlée; tandis que la grosse marmite soufflait des jets de vapeur comme une chaudière, les flancs secoués par des glouglous graves et profonds. | The back room was entirely lit by the three braziers; roux mixtures were giving off a burnt smell in the pans, with a heavy smoke of scorched flour, while the big pot puffed out jets of steam like a boiler, its sides shaken by deep, heavy gurgles. | zola-lassommoir-1877.txt:7729 |

| 5867 | impatroniser | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Tous deux venaient de loin en loin pour ne pas effaroucher mademoiselle Sylvie, ils causaient avec Rogron sous divers prétextes, et s’impatronisaient avec une réserve et des façons que le grand Tartufe eût admirées. | The two of them came around only now and then so as not to alarm Mademoiselle Sylvie; they would chat with Rogron under various pretexts, and made themselves at home with a discretion and manner the great Tartuffe himself would have admired. | Honoré de Balzac, Pierrette, 1840, d. 1850 |
| 5872 | queuter | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Quant à l'action de queuter ou de billarder, ce n'est pas trop, comme il est d'usage en France, de tenir pour nul le carambolage qu'on a pu faire ainsi; il serait même juste que le fauteur fût puni de la perte d'un point, car c'est une espèce de filouterie. | As for the act of pushing the ball or double-hitting it, it is not excessive, as is customary in France, to void any cannon shot made that way; indeed it would be fair for the offender to lose a point, since it is a kind of cheating. | Benjamin Pifteau, Grande encyclopédie générale des jeux, 1880, d. 1890 |
| 5879 | planchéier | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Rigou contempla, pour la millième fois, cette salle à manger, planchéiée en chêne, plafonnée à moulures, garnie de belles armoires bien peintes, boisée à hauteur d’appui, ornée d’un beau poêle et d’un cartel magnifique, provenus de Mlle Laguerre. | Rigou gazed once more at this dining room, floored in oak, its ceiling adorned with molding, furnished with fine well-painted cabinets, paneled up to shoulder height, and set off by a handsome stove and a magnificent mantel clock, both of which had come from Mademoiselle Laguerre. | Honoré de Balzac, Les Paysans, 1845, d. 1850 |

| 5889 | enfieller | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Ces jours-là, le cœur enfiellé d’une amère tristesse, il revenait au château, pâle, défait, abattu, comme un homme qui relève de maladie, et il restait silencieux des heures entières, assis, le menton dans la main, à l’angle de la cheminée. | On those days, his heart embittered by a bitter sadness, he would return to the château, pale, worn out, and dejected, like a man recovering from illness, and he would remain silent for hours on end, sitting with his chin in his hand, in the corner by the fireplace. | Théophile Gautier, Le capitaine Fracasse, 1863, d. 1872 |

| 5929 | scorifier | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Ils débouchèrent dans une nouvelle plaine, la Mer des Pluies, et là encore, en se postant sur une éminence, ils dominèrent un paysage fuyant à perte de vue, hérissé par des Alpes de plâtre, cabossé par des Etna de sel, gonflé de tubercules, boursouflé par des kystes, scorifié tel que du mâchefer. | They came out into a new plain, the Sea of Rains, and there again, standing on a rise, they looked out over a landscape stretching to the horizon — bristling with plaster Alps, dented by salt Etnas, swollen with tubers, puffed up with cysts, scorified like clinker. | Joris-Karl Huysmans, En rade, 1886, d. 1907 |

| 5949 | brouillasser | wiktionnaire | verbatim | Il s’était exempté de voisiner, en prétextant de ses occupations, de ses habitudes et de sa santé, qui ne lui permettaient pas, disait-il, de revenir la nuit par une route le long de laquelle brouillassait la Thune. | He had excused himself from socializing, citing his work, his habits, and his health, which he said did not let him come home at night along a road beside which the Thune lay under a drizzling mist. | Honoré de Balzac, Les Paysans, 1845, d. 1850 |

| 5978 | détortiller | wiktionnaire | verbatim | À huit heures et demi, au moment où son ancien commis passait sa robe de chambre et secouait les idées confuses du réveil, bâillait, se détortillait, demandait pardon à son ancien patron, Birotteau se trouva face à face avec le tigre affamé de vengeance dans lequel il voulait voir son seul ami. | At half past eight, just as his former clerk was putting on his dressing gown, shaking off the confused thoughts of waking, yawning, stretching himself out, and apologizing to his former employer, Birotteau found himself face to face with the tiger hungry for revenge in whom he wanted to see his only friend. | Honoré de Balzac, Histoire de la Grandeur et de la Décadence de César Birotteau, 1837, d. 1850 |

## Other checker notes

Notes on the 552 verbs not shown in a section above. They mostly explain why a candidate sentence was passed over.

- **obtenir** (57): gloss_lint flags a duplicate_gloss against sortir ('obtain'), which allegedly shares no English sense with sortir — that concern belongs to sortir's entry, not this one; obtenir's own gloss is correct
- **commencer** (68): gloss_lint flags a duplicate_gloss against débucher — that concern belongs to débucher's entry, not this one; commencer's own gloss is correct
- **reprendre** (141): 'reprendre' is also very commonly used for 'to resume/carry on with' (WT sense 3), which the gloss does not spell out; not flagged as a defect since 'take back' is a defensible primary rendering.
- **accorder** (227): gloss_lint flags this gloss as a duplicate of octroyer's gloss; both mean 'grant' and share no other English sense in this shard's evidence, so no change is proposed, but it's worth Josh's awareness that two verbs read identically to VoiceOver.
- **analyser** (254): gloss_lint's no_overlap flag looks spurious: it compares "analyze" against "analyse" and finds no literal overlap, but the senses are identical.
- **taire** (277): The shipped example uses the reflexive form "se taisait" (be silent); this is a genuine verbal use of the verb and reads naturally under the gloss "keep quiet" even though the entry's re flag is false (non-pronominal-only).
- **mourir** (292): audits.gloss_lint flags this gloss as a duplicate of décéder's gloss 'die'; both are accurate but the app may want to distinguish register (mourir is neutral, décéder is formal/administrative)
- **employer** (334): gloss_lint flagged 'employer' as sharing an identical gloss with 'utiliser'; both genuinely mean 'use' in French and the overlap is not an error, just informational.
- **personnaliser** (396): gloss_lint's no_overlap finding for this verb appears to be a false positive caused by British/American spelling mismatch (personalise vs. personalize), not a real gloss defect.
- **dresser** (481): Example illustrates the reflexive 'se dresser' (stand up/straighten), a sense adjacent to but not literally named by 'build, set, tame'; kept as ok since it is the reflexive counterpart of the 'raise, erect' sense.
- **coûter** (505): gloss_lint flags this gloss as identical to the entry for 'couter' (no circumflex), which is a different, unrelated word; that duplication looks like a bug on the 'couter' entry rather than this one.
- **brûler** (596): gloss_lint flags duplicate_gloss with 'bruler' (unaccented); this looks like a spelling-variant entry rather than a real duplicate, but worth a human check.
- **abonner** (617): gloss_lint flags duplicate_gloss with 'souscrire'; both can mean 'subscribe' but are distinct verbs with different registers, not a real duplicate. · Rejected the first two tier candidates: one uses 'abonnés' adjectivally ('utilisateurs abonnés') and starts mid-quotation with a stray »; the other has a footnote digit fused onto the text ('CO2/an6').
- **désoler** (657): the audits.flags evidence for this verb ('no sense tagged pronominal in either edition') appears to be incorrect — both Wiktionnaire and English Wiktionary do tag a pronominal/reflexive sense
- **généraliser** (660): gloss_lint's no_overlap and duplicate_gloss (with vulgariser) flags look like false positives caused by American/British spelling mismatch, not a real gloss defect
- **souscrire** (666): gloss_lint flags this as an identical gloss to abonner though the two verbs share no English sense; worth distinguishing but not a defect in this entry alone.
- **coucher** (668): coucher also has strong non-pronominal uses (transitive 'put to bed', intransitive 'sleep, spend the night'), so re=true reflects only the sense the gloss leads with, per the one-value-per-verb rule.
- **téléphoner** (779): All tier candidates use 'téléphone' as the noun (telephone/by phone), never the verb; the wiktionary_en usage example is a genuine verbal use and was used instead.
- **hacher** (855): The chosen quotation (Zola, Le Docteur Pascal, 1893, death_year 1902) is public domain and uses 'hacher' as a noun-modifying infinitive ('table à hacher'); reviewed as an acceptable, natural sentence, though a tier candidate with a more central verbal use ('se ferait hacher en morceaux') was also available and could be substituted if a more prototypical verb form is preferred.
- **différencier** (879): gloss_lint notes this gloss is identical to différentier's, though the audit says the two share no English sense; not itself an error, but worth a second look if the two entries are ever confused in the app.
- **faillir** (900): audits.conjugations shows the app's imperative secondSingular form for faillir as 'faUX', which looks like a garbled/miscapitalized engine artifact rather than a real form (Wiktionary has 'faillis'); worth checking as a possible real bug.
- **coupler** (914): The source sentence has a stray footnote digit glued onto the date ('202014'); rendered here as '2020', the correct reading, since the digit is plainly an extraction artifact and not part of the sentence.
- **plier** (925): The example uses the fixed idiom 'plier bagage' (pack up and leave); it is covered loosely by the 'fold up' sense and by wiktionnaire's untagged 'emballer, empaqueter', so it was left as ok, but a learner may need the idiom explained separately.
- **amplifier** (941): The two earlier war/cyberattack candidates and the hyphen-corrupted 'Direc- tion' candidate were rejected as impenetrable without context or visibly corrupted, respectively.
- **configurer** (943): gloss_lint flags this as a duplicate_gloss of 'paramétrer', which shares no English sense with it; the two entries may be worth differentiating (e.g. 'configure' vs 'set the parameters of') if both remain in the app.
- **allouer** (946): The first two 'allouer' candidates are cut off (trailing '(cf.' and a stray leading '4,'); rejected as truncated.

## Appendix: refuted items

| Rank | Verb | Task | Proposed | Severity | Skeptic’s reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 78 | sortir (obtain) | gloss | — | hedge | The checker proposes no replacement (proposed is null). The entry is the deliberate homograph: its id is 'sortir (obtain)' and its -iss- conjugations (sortissait, sortissant) match the attested 'sortissant son plein et entier effet'. 'obtain' matches Wiktionnaire's 'Obtenir, avoir.' exactly, so a duplicate_gloss with obtenir is expected for this entry. At most it could take a register label such as '(obsolete)'. |
| 125 | atteindre | gloss | reach, attain | nitpick | 'attain' is English Wiktionary's first untagged sense and correctly covers Wiktionnaire's 'Parvenir à un terme'. The claim that 'reach' is commoner is an appeal to frequency with no evidence behind it, and adding a correct synonym to a correct gloss fixes nothing wrong. |
| 129 | éviter | gloss | avoid, dodge, avert | nitpick | All five words are verbatim, untagged English Wiktionary senses ('to avoid', 'to dodge, to shun, to bypass', 'to avert'), and five single words are short enough to read aloud. The 'two or three senses' limit the checker cites is not house style, so the current gloss is not wrong. |
| 180 | exercer | gloss | practice, exercise, instruct | hedge | The evidence misquotes the sources. Wiktionnaire leads with 'Dresser, former, instruire à quelque chose par des actes fréquents', and 'Pratiquer' is its fifth sense, tagged 'broadly'. English Wiktionary's 'to instruct, to command' has no 'dated' tag. The reordering rests on claims the shard contradicts. |
| 199 | profiter | gloss | take advantage of, benefit | nitpick | The current senses are not redundant. 'make the most of' is English Wiktionary's first sense ('to take advantage of, make the most of, enjoy'), which carries the everyday 'profiter de ses vacances', and the proposal drops it. Nine words are readable, and the current gloss is correct. |
| 231 | convenir | gloss | admit, agree, suit | nitpick | The current gloss copies wiktionary_en word for word ('to admit; to agree', 'to suit; to be convenient for') and nothing in it is wrong. Dropping three words for brevity only swaps one correct gloss for another. |
| 275 | évoluer | gloss | evolve, change, develop | nitpick | 'to play' and 'to move (in a given area), to move about' are untagged senses in wiktionary_en, and Wiktionnaire also lists 'Se déplacer, se mouvoir' and 'Jouer'. The proposal would drop live, correct senses for brevity alone. |
| 310 | reposer | flag | re → no | hedge | The evidence misreads the shard: it says no sense is tagged pronominal, but wiktionary_en tags 'to rest, to repose' as reflexive, and Wiktionnaire tags 'Cesser de travailler… pour faire disparaître la fatigue' as pronominal. That is the 'rest' sense the gloss leads with. Showing that non-reflexive senses also exist does not prove the shipped value wrong for the lead sense. |
| 359 | résulter | flag | dg → change the defect group (see evidence) | hedge | Neither edition marking a verb defective does not show the verb is fully conjugated. Wiktionnaire's 'S’ensuivre' sense is itself tagged 'impersonal', and the only first-person evidence is a jokey internet quote ('je résulte de la fusion de Lust et Gluttony'). The proposal also names no replacement defect group. |
| 373 | affecter | gloss | affect, influence, feign | hedge | The shipped 'feign, affect' matches en Wiktionary's first sense 'to feign, affect (an emotion, etc.)'. The checker's reordering rests only on an unsupported frequency claim, at low confidence. Wiktionnaire leads with neither sense ('Destiner et appliquer…'), so the evidence does not support 'affect, influence' as the lead sense. |
| 398 | résoudre | example | wrong_sense: — | hedge | The fault is in the gloss, not the example. Proust's 'Je résolus de m'abstenir' uses the 'resolve' sense, which the corrected gloss 'solve, resolve' covers, and Proust (d. 1922) is public domain. Replacing a valid corpus citation with an authored sentence is unwarranted. |
| 398 | résoudre | new_example | Les ingénieurs ont mis plusieurs jours à résoudre ce problème technique complexe. | hedge | The authored sentence is grammatical, but it exists only because the example was judged against the broken gloss 'dissolve'. Against gloss_proposed 'solve, resolve', the shipped Proust sentence ('Je résolus de…') already qualifies, so an authored replacement is not needed. |
| 495 | repérer | gloss | spot, detect, pick out | nitpick | Both references lead with the mark sense: wiktionary_en 'to map out, to mark, to reference' and wiktionnaire 'Marquer, indiquer des repères.' The proposal drops that sense entirely, and its only support for putting 'spot' first is an unsupported frequency claim. The shipped gloss is correct and verbatim. |
| 499 | parcourir | gloss | go through, skim | nitpick | The shipped gloss is correct and copies wiktionary_en's two senses ('to go through, to pass through' and 'to read through, to skim'). At four short items it is easy to read aloud, and a length lint by itself does not make a correct gloss wrong. |
